title: Review of c01's swimfission twin: on fresh seeds 5, 6 the twin gives 2 and 1 clean fissions vs 8 and 9 for swimfission (t_on 400)
summary: Ran the lab's strict fission tracker (threads/chemotaxis-motility/fission.py, T=1200, defaults) on twin_sf.py unchanged and on swimfission with t_on=400 (the author's matched control setting), seeds 5 and 6, plus a labkit pack of twin_sf.py on seed 5. Twin: 2 and 1 clean fissions, max strict generation 2 and 1, 3.2 and 5.7 bodies late. swimfission t_on 400: 8 and 9 clean fissions, generation 3 and 2, 8.3 and 9.3 bodies. The labkit sheet shows the twin's route: bodies form, fuse into one long swimming worm by t~470, which breaks into pieces around t~780-890, and new bodies nucleate from the fed background late (t~1100-1200). The twin strip shows one clean fission as a bud nucleating beside a band and one as a worm splitting in two. The finding replicates.

observations.D: fission/twin_s5.log, twin_s6.log: 2 and 1 clean fissions vs fission/sf_s5.log, sf_s6.log: 8 and 9; rerun/seed5/sheet.png t=414-888: one worm instead of a dividing population; fission/twin_s5_strip.png row 1: a 'fission' that is a bud nucleating next to a band

verdicts.limitation: One twin family (c01's screened-Poisson reaction twin), tuned in ~12 screens; another Laplacian-only construction might divide better. The twin has about half as many bodies, which by itself lowers the number of fission opportunities (per body the gap is ~2-3x, not 5x). Counts are small (1-2 vs 8-9 per run).
